geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Cut a circle into wedges and form a "parallelogram".

Goal: I can derive A = (pi)r^2 by slicing and rearranging.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Area of a circle: A = πr2.

Cut a circle into many equal wedges and arrange them alternately point up and point down. The shape looks more and more like a parallelogram with height r and base half the circumference, πr. Its area is πr times r = πr2.

The same follows from regular polygons: A = (1/2)aP, and as n grows the apothem approaches r and the perimeter approaches 2πr, so the area approaches (1/2)(r)(2πr) = πr2.
